rationale: The page is a standard e-commerce/pharmacy landing page. There is a prominent navigation bar at the top with a search bar. A side menu provides primary navigation (Overview, Shop medicines, Prescription, etc.). The main content area features a personalized greeting ('Good morning, Alex 👋') and a strong call-to-action: 'Better health starts with the right care.' followed by an 'Explore medicines →' button. Further down, there are categorized shopping options (All products, Pain relief, Vitamins, etc.) and a section for 'Popular products' with listings.. To conduct a thorough usability and journey audit, I need to see the entirety of the page content, especially the bottom sections of 'Popular products' and any potential footer elements, to evaluate the overall layout consistency and readability. [Friction observed: For a novice user with low vision, the side menu uses small icons next to text, and the general layout can feel a bit busy. The contrast between some text elements and the white background needs careful review, though the primary text seems legible. The category buttons are good touch targets, but the initial navigation structure requires the user to scan several options.]
